item.description: The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 32 miles south of Cairo, when a train traveling to the southwestern Fayoum province crashed into the rear of another train.

item.title: Calley Means says Trump "has been subverted by people that are beholden to special interests"
item.description: Calley Means, the former White House senior adviser and aide to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. who resigned last month, told "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" that he believes "President Trump has been subverted by people that are beholden to special interests and not what President Trump ran on, and what voters voted for."

item.title: Trump on allegations he's profiting from the presidency
item.description: Ross Douthat asks the President how his net worth rose by nearly $3 billion, according to a Forbes estimate, since he returned to office. Watch the interview Sunday at 7 p.m. ET/PT on 60 Minutes.

item.title: "The Altruists" actor Julia Garner on surprising herself
item.description: In "The Altruists," the Emmy-winning star of "Ozark" plays Caroline Ellison, girlfriend of Sam Bankman-Fried and business partner in a multi-billion-dollar cryptocurrency fraud. Julia Garner talks about how, for her, the eyes truly are the windows to the soul.

item.title: ICE unlikely to scale back crackdown, sources say, citing Stephen Miller
item.description: The Trump administration is unlikely to scale back its aggressive crackdown on illegal immigration following the results of the midterm elections, multiple U.S. officials told CBS News, citing the elevation of Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff.

item.title: Full interview: Rep.-elect Nancy Lacore, former Navy Vice Admiral fired by Sec. Hegseth
item.description: Watch Margaret Brennan's full interview with Rep.-elect Nancy Lacore, a portion of which aired on Nov. 8. Rep.-elect Lacore will become the highest-ranking female U.S. military officer to ever serve in Congress. She served as chief of the Naval Reserve until she was let go by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth without explanation in August 2025. Rep.-elect Lacore was one of more than three dozen candidates who flipped their seats in last week's "blue wave."

item.title: OC fishermen find cruise ship employee treading water miles off coast
item.description: Two Newport Beach fishermen found a Royal Caribbean cruise ship employee treading water nearly 20 miles off the coast while returning home from a fishing trip near Catalina Island on Friday.

item.title: Rep.-elect Nancy Lacore says she was "never given a reason" why Pete Hegseth fired her
item.description: Rep.-elect Nancy Lacore told "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" that she was "never given a reason" why Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired her as a chief of the Navy Reserve, but she added that "at this point, it doesn't really matter. You know, it opened a door for me to do what I'm doing now and continuing my service in Congress."

item.title: Trump says U.S. took a "giant step back in history" with midterm results
item.description: President Trump on Sunday said the U.S. "took a giant step back in history" as his White House continued to roil from his post-midterm shakeup

item.title: GOP Rep. French Hill says "I want to hear the debate" on impeaching Pete Hegseth
item.description: As outgoing Rep. Thomas Massie plans to force a vote on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Republican Rep. French Hill said he "I want to hear the debate on it to see if it merits impeachment versus some other disciplinary action or action by the president, if he's not getting the job done in leading the Department of War."

item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Sen. Elizabeth Warren says scammers "better get ready for some investigations, serious ones"
item.description: With Democrats taking control of both legislating and oversight in Congress, Sen. Elizabeth Warren says "if you've been making your profits by cheating American families and scamming your investors, you better get ready for some investigations, serious ones." When asked to elaborate if she had anyone in mind, Warren said "anyone who's been cheating."

item.title: With "Thrasher," Brandon Flowers returns home
item.description: Smalltown Nephi, Utah, was where the musical sensibilities of Killers frontman Brandon Flowers started to take form, before finding success as a rock star in Las Vegas. Now his solo album, "Thrasher," is filled with country songs like those beloved by his dad.

item.title: With "Thrasher," Brandon Flowers returns home
item.description: Small town Nephi, Utah, was where the musical sensibilities of Brandon Flowers, frontman of The Killers, started to take form, before being seduced by the bright lights of Las Vegas. Now he's released his third solo album, "Thrasher," filled with country-western songs like those beloved by his dad. Flowers talks with correspondent Luke Burbank about storytelling, family, and what true success feels like.

item.title: Jon Meacham on the midterms and America's "better angels"
item.description: In last week's historic elections, voters were asked to weigh in on whether our nation will maintain the ideals of equality, dignity, fair play, and the rule of law; historian Jon Meacham says that Americans overwhelmingly answered, and democracy prevailed.

item.description: The celebrated actress' latest book – conversations with friend and fellow actor Brendan O'Hea – revisits an extraordinary career and a remarkable life, from Shakespeare to Bond.
